title: A safe copy function is only safe if the bound is the destination's size, not the input's length
index_line: T-0054 · MEM_WRITE · strncpy(dest, src, strlen(src)) into a 256-byte stack buffer, pre-auth · c/cpp · corroborated
invariant_violated: Choosing the bounded copy instead of the unbounded one is treated as having handled the problem — a reviewer sees strncpy and moves on. But the third argument is the destination's capacity, and the code passed the source's length. The function was made safe in name and left exactly as dangerous in the one way that matters.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated client opens a session and supplies a protocol field whose length it chooses
the handler measures the field with the standard length function and stores the value with its length
the copy is issued into a fixed stack buffer using the measured source length as the bound
the bound exceeds the destination, so the write continues past the buffer into adjacent stack variables
the overwrite reaches the saved return address, and control flow is redirected

source.protocol.value: a binary protocol field negotiated before authentication — the length is the payload, the content is filler

sink.memory.copy.value: the bounded-copy call whose third argument is the wrong quantity

size.length.value: the measured source length standing in for the destination capacity — the single swapped operand

preconditions.expr: the handler is reachable before authentication

check.spec: timeout 5 nc HOST PORT </dev/null | head -c 120; echo; echo 'reachable if bytes returned'

preconditions.expr: a bounded copy is called with a source-derived length instead of the destination's size

spec.method: compare the vulnerable and fixed binaries around the handler; a changed copy-length operand is the tell

success: the service crashes or gains control flow from a single oversized field with no authentication
the crashing copy's length equals the supplied field length in a debugger
the same request with a short field is inert
failure_like: the length is clamped or compared against the destination size before the copy
false_positive: a crash in a different handler caused by malformed framing — confirm the faulting instruction is the copy
a crash that needs authentication first — that is a post-auth bug and changes the severity entirely

hazards: grep for the bounded functions and read the third argument; strncpy with a source length is the most common false sense of safety in C
strlcpy and snprintf also take the destination size — the same swapped-operand mistake defeats them
this is a pre-auth overflow on an edge appliance, so the patch window is the exposure window
distinct from T-0010 (attacker length sizing an allocation) and T-0041 (decoder output extent): here the code intended to bound and bounded the wrong thing
non_transfers: code that passes the destination size (the intended use)
languages where the copy carries both lengths
